title: S&P Global PMI Commodity Price & Supply Indicators (Oct 2026 data) — 11:00 ET, an hour after the US manufacturing final
source: EST: read verbatim off S&P Global's own calendar listing, pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en, fetched direct 2026-10-26 with a browser User-Agent (HTTP 200, 26,777 bytes): 'November 02 ... 16:00 UTC S&P Global PMI Commodity Price & Supply Indicators'. 16:00 UTC is 11:00 EST once US daylight time ends 2026-11-01 (the 10-01 release of the same series sat at 15:00 UTC = 11:00 EDT). Filed estimate on the standing schema gap for a private PMI compiler, not on date doubt. Re-read first-hand by the initial-research lane 2026-10-26 (same fetch: calendar HTTP 200, 26,777 bytes; the press-release index, HTTP 200, 89,736 bytes, carries the realized 10-01 instance of this series, whose PDF masthead reads 'Embargoed until 1100 EDT (1500 UTC) 1 October 2026'). The calendar's own stated rules name only Manufacturing, Services and Whole Economy PMIs, so this series' first-working-day cadence is inferred from its realized instances, not stated. Checked 2026-10-26
notes: READ IT, DO NOT TRADE IT. The September edition (10-01, primary PDF re-read 2026-10-26) ended a five-month easing run: All Items Price Pressures 2.0 (Aug 1.9), energy 4.5x, transport 6.3x the long-run average, semiconductors moderating to 13.1x from August's four-year peak, electrical-items shortages 4.6x (worst since Feb 2023). The October edition's collection window (expected ~12-26 Oct 2026, not yet published) sits in a higher oil tape than September's: Brent $102.31 (10-01) -> $109.86 (10-16) -> $110.10 (10-20, five-month high, Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure, ~18 vessels attacked in two weeks per press reports). Medium-confidence read: energy price pressure rises again; headline less certain because semiconductors are easing. Release lands 11:00 ET (16:00 UTC, EST) on 11-02, the day after the 11-01 OPEC+ meeting and in the same corridor as ISM Manufacturing, SLOOS, construction spending and the AAPL print. No consensus is published for any index in this series; symbols is empty and no house playbook is macro-keyed. Full ledger: docs/research/events/sp-global-pmi-commodity-price-supply-2026-11-02.md.
